subject: MSA: Liability cap & gross negligence carve-out
messages:

Date: 2026-03-02T16:12:00Z
Subject: MSA redline - liability cap / gross negligence carve-out

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached is our MSA redline with comments on Section 7 (Limitation of Liability) and Section 12 (Indemnities). Two specific asks from our legal team:

- Confirm whether Redwood will accept a gross negligence/willful misconduct carve-out that is limited to "intentional fraud" or whether the carve-out will include gross negligence as a standalone exception.
- Propose an acceptable liability cap: our procurement needs an explicit monetary cap tied to contract value. We currently have a floor of $10M for strategic vendors; can Redwood provide options (e.g., aggregate fees, fixed monetary cap, or multiple-of-fees)?

We want to keep momentum on the Order Form but need clarity on those points before we proceed to signature. Copying Megan (external counsel) for any redline suggestions.

Attachments: Acme_MSA_redline_from_Acme.docx (tracked changes)

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corp

Subject: Re: MSA redline - liability cap / gross negligence carve-out

Jordan —

Appreciate the clean redline. Routing this to our legal and procurement partners to give you a considered answer. High-level thoughts for context while they review:

- Redwood’s standard position: cap liability to the greater of (i) aggregate fees paid in prior 12 months or (ii) $5M for hosted contracts. We can be flexible for strategic customers.
- On carve-outs: we typically exclude fraud and willful misconduct from caps; gross negligence is negotiable but we try to narrow the definition (e.g., require a material breach + objective recklessness) so the exception isn’t open-ended.

I’ll get back with a redline proposal by end of week. In the meantime, sending along our current proposed MSA with a targeted change set so you can see precise language.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_redline_v4.docx

Best,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-03-04T09:20:00Z
Subject: RE: MSA redline - liability cap / gross negligence carve-out

Team / Jordan —

Review completed. Key recommendations and rationale below (I’ve pasted proposed language in the tracked doc attached):

1) Cap formula: propose "Cap" = greater of (i) aggregate fees paid under the Order Form in the 12 months immediately preceding the claim, or (ii) $7,500,000. Rationale: balances customer procurement expectations and business risk for hosted inference. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can discuss higher, tiered caps.

2) Carve-outs: Redwood will accept an exclusion from the Cap for "willful misconduct" and "fraud". We recommend against an unconstrained gross negligence carve-out. Instead, if Acme insists on gross negligence, limit it as follows:
   - Gross negligence excluded from cap only where (a) the act/omission rises to the level of material breach of the MSA, and (b) the conduct demonstrates reckless disregard for contractual obligations.
   - Equivalent: add a two-part test (materiality + reckless standard) rather than subjective "gross negligence" wording. This narrows exposure and is defensible in court.

3) Consequential damages: Redwood remains intolerant of broad waivers; we propose maintaining a general exclusion of consequential, special, and punitive damages except where explicitly awarded for willful misconduct or proven fraud.

4) Minimum thresholds & notice: include a claim threshold (e.g., $50,000) and a 60-day cure period before gross negligence exception becomes actionable where material breach is alleged. This reduces nuisance claims.

5) Insurance & indemnity interplay: clarify that indemnities for third-party IP infringement are outside the Cap but subject to policy limits; cross-reference our insurance schedules.

Jordan/Megan: if your side can accept the two-part gross negligence restriction and a cap at the greater of 12-month fees or $7.5M, we can prepare a clean operating MSA and send for signature. If not, please indicate whether Acme needs a fixed $10M floor and we’ll escalate.

Attachments: internal_review_notes.pdf (legal commentary on carve-out language)

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

If Acme is classified as a strategic expansion account (we should confirm ARR and roadmap fit), I can approve a 2x uplift on the standard $7.5M cap (i.e., $15M) but would want this subject to:
- Deal desk sign-off (finance + legal)
- 12-month committed spend in the Order Form or an annual minimum commitment

Otherwise recommend sticking with the proposed 7.5M cap and the two-part gross negligence restriction.

Marissa / Rishi —

Appreciate the rapid review. A few follow-ups from Acme legal:

- Acme prefers a $10M floor (fixed) rather than a multiple-of-fees approach. Would Redwood accept a $10M fixed cap for strategic partners?
- On the two-part gross negligence test: we think objective thresholds are OK but need examples of what would satisfy "material breach" and "reckless disregard" in practice — can Redwood add clarifying language or examples?
- Timeline: if we can agree to language, procurement would like a signed MSA this month; please send the revised redline and any required internal approvals.

Also copying Priya (Procurement) for logistics.

Thanks,
Jordan

Subject: FINAL: Revised MSA redline & next steps

Jordan / Priya —

Thanks for the feedback and for the quick turnaround on procurement timing. Per the internal thread, please find attached our revised MSA (Redwood_MSA_redline_v4.docx) that: 

- Sets the Cap at the greater of (i) aggregate fees paid in the prior 12 months or (ii) $7,500,000 by default; for strategic customers we are open to a fixed $10M floor subject to Deal Desk approval (Neha will coordinate).
- Narrows gross negligence carve-out to a two-part test: (1) act/omission gives rise to a material breach of the MSA (materiality defined as a failure that reasonably impairs the purpose of the agreement), and (2) the behavior satisfies an objective "reckless disregard" standard (examples provided in the doc: repeated failure to remediate a known security vulnerability after notice; deliberate circumvention of usage controls).
- Adds a $50k claims threshold and a 60-day cure period before liability escalates to carve-out consideration.
- Leaves consequential damages excluded except where damages arise from willful misconduct or proven fraud.

Next steps: please review attached redline and confirm whether Acme can accept the two-part gross negligence language and the Cap structure. If you accept the $10M fixed floor, please indicate so and we’ll route to Deal Desk for approval and return a DocuSign envelope.
